nodes.label: Dependabot version-update configuration
nodes.rationale: CI gates ENFORCE (vulnerable dep fails build), Dependabot PROPOSES (opens the fixing PR); neither replaces the other. Updates are grouped so routine churn arrives as few reviewable PRs; security fixes deliberately ungrouped so an advisory fix is readable and mergeable on its own.

nodes.label: vite/vitest peer-locked major-bump group
nodes.rationale: The vite/vitest cluster is peer-locked to itself (@vitest/coverage-v8 pins vitest exactly; @vitejs/plugin-react and vitest pin vite ranges) so a solo major bump is unresolvable — ERESOLVE on npm ci, seen as #187/#189/#190. Majors must land as one PR.

nodes.label: NuGet vulnerability audit gate (high+, blocking)
nodes.rationale: dotnet list package --vulnerable always exits 0, so the JSON is parsed by vuln-gate.mjs. Runs after restore (needs the resolved graph) but before build so a vulnerable dep is caught even if compilation would fail. --output-version 1 pins the JSON schema against silent CLI shape changes.

nodes.label: npm production audit gate (high+, blocking)
nodes.rationale: npm audit exits non-zero on ANY severity; under pipefail that would let npm's exit, not the gate's threshold, decide the step. Output captured to a file (|| true) so the gate is the sole arbiter. --omit=dev scopes blocking to what ships to browsers; the full tree runs advisory-only. Exceptions path passed explicitly because the job runs from web/ and the default repo-root path would silently drop every npm exception.

nodes.label: Dependency review job (PR diff-scoped gate)
nodes.rationale: Needs the repo Dependency graph (owner toggle with no API). Probes the sbom endpoint: only a definitive 403/404 skips the review, with a loud warning naming the setting so it self-activates once toggled; a transient status still runs the review rather than silently disabling the gate.

nodes.label: --locked-mode deterministic restore (NU1004 on drift)
nodes.rationale: Restore must match committed packages.lock.json exactly so a dependency can't float to a different resolved version between a green local run and CI; fails NU1004 when a bump skipped regenerating locks.

nodes.label: vuln-gate.mjs shared vulnerability gate script
nodes.rationale: Self-tested with node:test before its verdict is trusted. Fails closed: malformed report, unknown severity, or malformed exception all block rather than pass. --emit-allowlist yields the live GHSA ids for dependency-review so the two gates never disagree.

nodes.label: CodeQL SAST workflow (csharp + javascript-typescript)
nodes.rationale: Advisory mode — findings annotate PRs but don't gate merges, so a false positive can't wedge unrelated PRs; gating is a branch-ruleset toggle needing no file change. build-mode none avoids coupling to a preview .NET 10 toolchain. queries: security-extended keeps wider security coverage but drops the quality bucket whose heuristics are false-positive noise. Weekly cron catches advisories landing in CodeQL's own query packs between commits.

nodes.label: Dependabot lockfix workflow (workflow_run auto-heal)
nodes.rationale: Runs on workflow_run so the job definition comes from the default branch, never the PR — the PR author cannot change what executes. Inert until merged; fails closed until the LOCKFIX_APP_* secrets exist. Concurrency never cancels in-progress (a cancel mid-push could leave no fix).

nodes.label: compute job — credential-free lock regeneration
nodes.rationale: Runs the untrusted restore with permissions: {} and persist-credentials: false, checked out at the immutable head SHA (not the movable branch — TOCTOU). Cache disabled (privileged workflow_run reading a PR-populated cache is a documented poisoning surface); restore into a throwaway NUGET_PACKAGES dir; pinned --configfile so a branch nuget.config can't add sources.

nodes.label: commit job — trusted push with GitHub App token
nodes.rationale: Holds contents: write but runs zero project code; classifier and allowlist come from the trusted default-branch checkout. Pushes non-force from the same immutable SHA — a built-in compare-and-swap: fast-forward only if the branch tip is unmoved.
nodes.norm_label: commit job — trusted push with github app token

nodes.label: Provenance gate (Dependabot-only job-level if)
nodes.rationale: Requires BOTH actor and triggering_actor == dependabot[bot] (a re-run keeps actor but changes triggering_actor), run_attempt == 1, the dependabot/nuget/ branch prefix, and a numeric head-repository id match (never a fork). Deliberately no conclusion == success gate — CI is failing with NU1004 exactly when the fix is needed.

nodes.label: lockfix-apply.sh trusted applicator script
nodes.rationale: Runs in the commit job with the write token but executes no project code — only git and file ops. Validates each artifact lock is a regular file and parses as JSON, applies onto the PR checkout, classifies, and non-force pushes only on a lock-only diff.

nodes.label: NuGet dependency submission workflow
nodes.rationale: GitHub's graph parses NuGet manifests but never packages.lock.json and doesn't derive NuGet transitives statically — it saw 20 direct PackageReferences of ~80 resolved, leaving the PR-scoped dependency-review gate blind to transitively introduced vulnerable packages. component-detection reads the restore output and submits the resolved graph (locked-mode, so it describes exactly the pinned versions). NuGet only: npm is already covered by package-lock.json parsing and re-submitting would create a competing source. The correlator makes the snapshot replace itself instead of accumulating.

nodes.label: Scheduled security audit workflow (weekly cron on main)
nodes.rationale: CI gates only fire on a PR or push, so an advisory against an untouched dependency goes unnoticed until the next PR — this runs the SAME gates on a Monday cron. Separate workflow rather than schedule: on ci.yml because it needs only the audits, not the build and 685 tests, so it stays cheap. Blocking so the run goes red and GitHub notifies; both ecosystems run under if: always() so one advisory can't hide the other's.
nodes.norm_label: scheduled security audit workflow (weekly cron on main)

nodes.label: Single-container single-origin deployment (API serves SPA)
nodes.rationale: API and built SPA ship as one container serving both from the same origin — no CORS, no version skew between app bundle and API.

nodes.label: Account > Farms > Houses > Flocks tenant hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Multi-tenant from the root so the system scales past a single farm; flock classification extensible via species, production_purpose, production_model rather than hardcoding layers.

nodes.label: Two-layer backup: CSV export + pg_dump
nodes.rationale: In-app CSV/zip export is for spreadsheets and offline copies, not a restore format; the pg_dump custom-format dump is the real disaster-recovery backup. -T is required because a pseudo-TTY would corrupt the binary dump. Dumps contain credential hashes and all tenants — store as secrets.

nodes.label: Static asset caching policy for content-hashed builds (#141)
nodes.rationale: /assets/* is immutable max-age=31536000 (content-hashed names never change bytes); index.html is no-cache (not no-store — conditional ETag requests still allowed) so a new deploy propagates immediately; /api/* carries no static cache header.

nodes.label: Cloudflare CDN-in-front topology
nodes.rationale: Proxy the whole domain (origin already emits correct Cache-Control) rather than splitting frontend onto a separate CDN origin. Must be Full (strict), not Full — plain Full skips origin-cert validation so an on-path attacker could intercept authenticated API traffic. Explicit Bypass-cache rule on /api/* as belt-and-braces; Cloudflare bot/DDoS shield is a partial mitigation — API-side per-IP rate limiting (#143) is the real control.

nodes.label: dev Postgres service (loopback :5432)
nodes.rationale: Dev dependencies only, so the API can be run/debugged from the IDE against a real database; credentials are local defaults, the API reads its connection string from user-secrets.

nodes.label: app service (API + SPA bundle)
nodes.rationale: RateLimiting__TrustedProxies pins the compose network CIDR so the auth rate limiter reads X-Forwarded-For only from traefik — without a trusted proxy it would key on traefik's IP and throttle all users as one client (#143). AllowedHosts pins the public hostname so a forged Host header is rejected while loopback keeps the healthcheck working (#144). Port bound to loopback only so the plaintext API never reaches the LAN.

nodes.label: traefik reverse-proxy service (prod profile)
nodes.rationale: Prod-only via compose profile so bare docker compose up serves the API directly on :8080; discovers the app by container label, not service name, so renames need no label changes.

nodes.label: lockfix.mjs classify()
nodes.rationale: Pure classifier of git status --porcelain -z against an EXACT 7-path allowlist, not a glob — an unexpected lock location must surface as foreign and abort. Exit codes 0 commit / 2 abort / 3 noop; any crash is treated as abort by the caller (a classifier that cannot tell must never green-light a commit). Kept out of YAML so it can be unit-tested, mirroring vuln-gate.mjs.

nodes.label: lockfix.mjs changedPaths()
nodes.rationale: NUL-delimited parsing so a path with a space is one field; takes every path a record names — target AND rename/copy source — so a rename whose target is a lock file can't smuggle a foreign source past the check.

nodes.label: Grace-window mint-on-retry idempotent refresh (#176)
nodes.rationale: A tab dying between sending a refresh and receiving the rotated cookie leaves the old token in the cookie; the next tab's presentation reads as replay and nukes the family. The grace window makes refresh idempotent for the immediately-previous rotation. Unavoidable trade-off: within the window a stolen token is also accepted — mitigated by keeping it tiny (10s vs ~15-min cadence) and failing strict everywhere else. Deliberate design decision, 2026-07-23.

nodes.label: Refresh-token reuse detection (family revoke on divergence)
nodes.rationale: Catches divergence: a token derived from an already-rotated ancestor means theft; the whole token family is revoked.
nodes.norm_label: refresh-token reuse detection (family revoke on divergence)

nodes.label: Leap-frog chain-extension hole + RevokedByGrace fix
nodes.rationale: Naive grace let a stolen token be stepped down the chain (T0->grace->T2, T1->grace->T3, ...) extending a session indefinitely. RefreshToken.RevokedByGrace marks links revoked BY a grace-advance; TryGraceReplacementAsync refuses to grace such a link, bounding grace to a single hop; a second hop hits the strict theft path. Found by the 4-way review.

nodes.label: ConcurrencyStamp compare-and-swap on token consumption
nodes.rationale: RefreshToken had no concurrency control: two parallel presentations both minted live children — a fork that on the grace path spawned multiple sessions and skipped the family-revoke backstop. A regenerated ConcurrencyStamp makes consuming a token an atomic CAS; the loser's SaveChanges throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException and fails closed. Revoke paths became bulk ExecuteUpdateAsync so they don't fight the stamp. Invariant: never more than one live tip. Plus a clock-skew guard (elapsed >= 0).

nodes.label: Privilege separation: restore and write credential never coexist
nodes.rationale: dotnet restore is msbuild -t:Restore — Directory.Build.props/.targets, InitialTargets, restore-hooked targets, nuget.config credential providers and global.json SDK resolvers can all execute code during restore with no build step; checkout writes the token into .git/config by default, so restore-time code in the same job could exfiltrate it. 'PackageReference runs no install.ps1' only rules out legacy packages.config scripts. Hence the two-job split is the actual security control; the post-restore file check is data hygiene, not a boundary.
nodes.norm_label: privilege separation: restore and write credential never coexist

nodes.label: GitHub App token push (re-triggers CI)
nodes.rationale: A GITHUB_TOKEN push does not trigger another workflow run (recursion prevention), leaving the required check stuck at 'Expected — waiting for status'. A GitHub App installation token is short-lived, repo-scoped, contents:write only; the App bot's login != dependabot[bot] so the re-triggered run is gated out (loop-safe). A fine-grained PAT would work but is long-lived and account-bound — rejected.

nodes.label: Project reference chain Domain<-Application<-Infrastructure<-Api<-tests
nodes.rationale: Dependabot regenerates only the bumped project's lock (dependabot-core#5461); every downstream lock still pins the old transitive graph, so --locked-mode fails downstream. Intrinsic to keeping lock files on projects in a reference chain — dropping the locks would gut the reproducibility guarantee.

nodes.label: Save pending states design v3 (#236)
nodes.rationale: A multi-second save is indistinguishable from a dead button (only opacity .5); busy mechanisms were hand-rolled three ways and one form had no guard at all. Two shared pieces; risky per-screen logic (idempotency keys, refresh-before-rotate) deliberately stays where it was already reviewed.

nodes.label: Confirm-dialog handoff model
nodes.rationale: useConfirm settles before the caller's request starts, so dialog buttons never own in-flight I/O; once the confirmed request is in flight the dialog is gone and the originating row control is the pending indicator. Specified as observable state and tested with async queries rather than commit-order assumptions.

nodes.label: Bird Movement Ledger (Mortality/Cull/Adjustment)
nodes.rationale: Append-only; mortality rows are generated by daily-entry submission, never entered by hand (would double-count); corrections are new rows, ledger rows never edited or deleted. Current birds = initial count minus sum of movements, computed never stored.

nodes.label: Flock Lifecycle (Active/Depleted/Archived)
nodes.rationale: Active accepts everything; Depleted accepts backfill only up to depletion date (final laying days entered late); Archived accepts nothing and hides from pickers; Reactivate clears lifecycle dates restoring full capture.

nodes.label: Daily Entry Lifecycle (#69)
nodes.rationale: Draft → Submitted → Locked → ManagerAdjusted/Voided. Submitting atomically generates egg lots (with DailyEntryId link) and a mortality movement. Adjust reconciles lots in the same transaction, never below what a lot already sold, with compensating bird movements and audit snapshots. Void empties every generated lot (refused if eggs sold), reverses mortality, and vacates the day so the natural key can be reused — uniqueness enforced only across live entries (#82).

nodes.label: Egg Movement Ledger (#101)
nodes.rationale: Every change to a lot's available quantity is an explicit append-only signed row (Production/Sale/Void/Adjustment) written in the same transaction as the lot change, so cached QuantityAvailable always equals the sum of the lot's movements.

nodes.label: FIFO Allocation
nodes.rationale: Confirming a sale draws eggs from the oldest lots of that grade first under a pessimistic row lock so two sales can never allocate the same physical eggs. Void returns quantities to the exact lots they were drawn from, preserving FIFO order and withdrawal restrictions.

nodes.label: Operational Day (farm-local dates)
nodes.rationale: Dates are farm-local calendar dates resolved from the farm's timezone, not UTC (#35, #155). One boundary for every date rule — withdrawal, future-date guards, deplete/archive stamps, report windows — so a lot can never be sellable on one screen and restricted on another. On a UTC boundary a Los Angeles farm's restricted lot would read available a day early; genuinely future days are refused outright. Every capture picker opens on the farm's today (#123); only feed-lot expiry and History/Water range filters stay uncapped because a future date is their point.

nodes.label: Session Tokens (#145/#169/#176)
nodes.rationale: Access token (15 min) lives only in SPA JS memory (no durable credential for XSS); refresh token is an HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict cookie path-scoped to /api/v1/auth. Cross-tab refresh serialised via Web Locks (#169) because both tabs share one cookie and the second would trip theft-detection. A tiny (10s) single-hop idempotency grace (#176) treats a just-rotated token whose replacement is still live as a benign retry; consuming a token is an atomic compare-and-swap so replays can't fork sessions.
nodes.community_name: SPA Auth Flow (memory token + cookie refresh)

nodes.label: Auth Rate Limiting (#143)
nodes.rationale: Anonymous auth endpoints throttled per client IP: login strictly (10/15min), refresh loosely (60/15min — it carries legitimate automatic session traffic so must not share login's budget). 429 + Retry-After; real IP from reverse proxy X-Forwarded-For with trusted-proxy config.

nodes.label: Account Lockout (#128)
nodes.rationale: Complement to per-IP rate limiting, working per account: repeated failed logins (default 5) lock the account for 15 min. Reply stays the same generic 'Invalid email or password' (PBKDF2 still paid) so neither account existence nor lockout state leaks. Rate limiting blunts a spray across accounts from one address; lockout blunts a focused guess at one account from many addresses.

nodes.label: Farm Settings (#123)
nodes.rationale: Timezone, locale, currency, unit system + optional first-day-of-week and format overrides, on one Setup screen. Timezone is fully wired (decides the operational day); locale/unit system/format overrides are stored and validated but nothing renders through them yet — recorded now so the i18n display work (#45) has settings to read rather than a migration to run. Unresolvable timezones and region-less locales are refused outright.

nodes.label: Currency Change Rule (spec §4.6, extended)
nodes.rationale: Farm currency changes only while no amount at all is written down — no orders, payments, expenses, priced products, or feed money — because every recorded row keeps its currency forever and a catalog price is worse than stale: an order line taking it re-labels the raw number with the order's currency ($12.34 sold as ¥1,234). The API refuses the whole save, not just the field. When allowed, symbol and minor unit re-derive from the standard (JPY 0, KWD 3, unknown falls back to the code + 2 decimals).

nodes.label: Farm Logo (#123)
nodes.rationale: PNG/JPEG/WebP only, still images, 2 MB default cap, 4096px a side. SVG refused because it is a document that can carry script rendered back to every user; animated formats refused because an animated frame can hide data where the cleaning pass never looks. The image is taken apart and rebuilt to drop EXIF metadata (a phone photo carries the farm's GPS coordinates) and anything appended past the image's end; format decided by sniffing bytes, dimensions read from the header before decode.

nodes.label: Farm Palette (curated accent set)
nodes.rationale: Farm-wide accent colour chosen by an admin from a curated set (Aubergine, Forest, Slate, Terracotta); independent of per-user night mode. Curated rather than free-form because every palette ships a contrast-checked light and dark pair — an arbitrary colour cannot be held to that bar.

nodes.label: Version Concurrency Token
nodes.rationale: Every mutable aggregate carries a Version bumped by each mutation; second concurrent save gets a 409 and retries against fresh state. Append-only aggregates don't need one. Also the edit-in-place guard for water usage and expenses.

nodes.label: Audit Log (#93)
nodes.rationale: Append-only record of every corrective/destructive/configuration change: actor snapshot, UTC timestamp, action code, entity ref, reason, details. Domain data, not telemetry — written in the same transaction as the change so a rollback erases the event with it; no update or delete surface anywhere. Entity-local snapshots (AdjustedFromJson) remain as the record's own history.

nodes.label: Ledger-First Inventory Principle
nodes.rationale: Never directly edit a stock balance; every change is a movement row. Cached balances are allowed only if rebuildable from movement ledgers. Applies to egg lots, feed, supplements, medications, vaccines, packaging, bedding, future meat lots and bird allocations.

nodes.label: Egg Traceability Chain
nodes.rationale: The system must answer Sale → sales_order_item → egg allocations → egg_lot → flock → house → production_date → daily_entry.

nodes.label: Product-Generic Sales Model
nodes.rationale: Sales order items reference product_id; product-specific allocation tables (egg lots, future bird/meat lots) handle inventory source so future poultry modules plug in without redesigning the sales tables. One canonical model; the old egg-only sales_order_items schema was removed in v4.

nodes.label: Egg Lot
nodes.rationale: Egg Lot = farm + house + flock + production_date + egg_grade + location + quantity. Source of truth for egg inventory; dashboards aggregate but lots are canonical. Created only by submitting a daily entry.

nodes.label: Egg Inventory Movements Ledger
nodes.rationale: Append-only signed rows (production/sale/adjustment/discard/internal_use/transfer/reconciliation/void, plus grade_out/grade_in reserved) explaining every egg lot balance change.

nodes.label: Egg Unit Conversions (packed units)
nodes.rationale: No implicit fixed factor: a carton is 12, 18, or 30 eggs depending on market, so eggs-per-unit is farm-configurable. The factor is resolved at line creation and snapshotted on the sales order item (base_unit_factor) so redefining a unit never reinterprets recorded orders — same immutability principle as currency snapshots (§4.6). Missing active conversion blocks sale confirmation; never guess a factor.

nodes.label: Grading-at-Collection Assumption / Grade Transfers
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 assumes eggs are graded at collection; lot grade is fixed at production. Post-collection regrade/repack is reserved as egg_grade_transfers with paired grade_out/grade_in movements netting to zero eggs, because discarding from one lot and producing into another would corrupt the traceability chain (§9.6) and the discard ledger.

nodes.label: Hen-Day Production % KPI
nodes.rationale: eggs collected / hen-days on date x 100, using the point-in-time bird-ledger count of laying females (sex=female, production_purpose=layer), never the current post-mortality count (which inflates the rate). Mixed-sex flocks are flagged approximate (reserved female_bird_count upgrade path); period anchors to expected_start_lay_date and reports by week-of-lay for industry layer-curve comparability. Corrected in v4.4 from the wrong eggs/current-live-birds formula.

nodes.label: Sales Order Items (canonical schema)
nodes.rationale: Product-generic line: product_id, product_type_snapshot, quantity, unit, base_unit_factor snapshot, quantity_base (normalized: individual eggs for egg products), unit_price_cents, line_total_cents.

nodes.label: Sales Order Item Egg Allocations
nodes.rationale: Lot-level allocation rows (fifo/manual) linking a sales line to the egg lots it drew from; each carries the egg_inventory_movement it generated.

nodes.label: Egg-Lot Allocation Concurrency Rule
nodes.rationale: Sale confirmation serializes allocation: SELECT candidate egg_lots FOR UPDATE, re-read quantity_available, validate fit, insert allocations + movements, update cached balance, commit. Pessimistic lock is deliberate for a correctness-critical, short-lived, contended write so two sales can never allocate the same physical eggs; optimistic version fallback if row locks are unavailable.

nodes.label: Financial Row Currency Immutability
nodes.rationale: Financial rows must be self-contained for historical interpretation: sales_orders, payments, expenses snapshot currency_code + currency_minor_unit at creation and are always displayed from the row's stored fields, never the farm's current settings. Changing farm currency is blocked once financial rows exist; a farm truly changing currency gets a new farm record — history is never re-denominated.

nodes.label: Farm Localization Settings
nodes.rationale: Farm = currency + locale + timezone (+ unit system, first day of week, format overrides). Formatting and operational localization belong to the farm; UI language is the one exception — a per-user preference (users.language, BCP-47 primary subtag) with deterministic catalog resolution user language → default-farm locale language → English. Language never changes formatting.

nodes.label: Money as Integer Minor Units
nodes.rationale: Money is stored as integer minor units in the farm currency (USD 12.34 → 1234 with minor_unit 2; JPY 1200 → 1200 with minor_unit 0). Provider-neutral by construction.

nodes.label: Daily Entry (states, uniqueness, modular sections)
nodes.rationale: States draft/submitted/locked/manager_adjusted/voided; default lock after 7 farm-local days; UNIQUE(account, farm, house, flock, date); modular sections (core/egg/weight/breeding) shown by flock production_model; 60-second submit acceptance criterion (§8.5) for the normal egg-only path.

nodes.label: Bird Inventory Movements (bird ledger)
nodes.rationale: Append-only bird ledger (placement/mortality/cull/transfer/sale/harvest/adjustment/depletion/void). Current live birds = sum of quantity_delta; the ledger is canonical, not the starting-count arithmetic.

nodes.label: Medication Withdrawal Restriction
nodes.rationale: Egg lots produced while flock.active_egg_withdrawal_until >= production_date become restricted; restricted lots are hard-blocked from sale in Phase 1 (owner override deferred, with mandatory audit reason).

nodes.label: Write Idempotency Rule
nodes.rationale: Submitting the same draft twice must not duplicate lots or movements; uniqueness around reference_type + reference_id + movement_type plus table-specific constraints. Backbone of safe offline retry.

nodes.label: Unified Phase Plan
nodes.rationale: Phase 1.0 MVP (shipped 2026-07-16, epic #13): the smallest end-to-end egg loop — daily entry → egg lots → stock → sales order → FIFO allocation. Phase 1.1 hardening (roles, catalog, ledgers, feed/water, expenses, payments, reports, audit, export, i18n infra); 1.5 hardening + Spanish; 2-5 pullets/broilers/meat/breeder-hatchery.

nodes.label: Roles and Scope Model
nodes.rationale: Owner, Manager, Worker (assigned houses/flocks), Sales, Vet/Consultant, Read-only; workers scoped by assignment, financial reports hidden unless the role allows.

nodes.label: Vertical-Slice Architecture (KD-1)
nodes.rationale: .NET 10 Minimal APIs with each use case a self-contained slice (endpoint + handler + models + validators); cross-cutting concerns in shared middleware. No MediatR/AutoMapper ceremony: the build is solo + AI-assisted at modest scale and those libraries moved to commercial licenses; handlers are plain classes invoked directly.

nodes.label: Multi-Tenancy Enforcement (KD-3)
nodes.rationale: Shared schema with account_id discriminator enforced globally: TenantContext resolved from the JWT claim by middleware, EF global query filter on every entity so a missing WHERE can't leak data, SaveChanges interceptor stamps account_id on inserts, and cross-tenant isolation integration tests are required. SaaS later changes tenant resolution only — the data layer never changes.

nodes.label: Offline for Data Capture Only (KD-4)
nodes.rationale: Daily production capture queues offline; sales confirmation, allocation, reconciliation, payments, and withdrawal-setting medication stay online-only because anything allocating shared inventory or touching money cannot be optimistically applied offline — two devices could allocate the same physical eggs, resolvable only by a server holding a lock. Mirrors functional §8.5's fast-path scoping.

nodes.label: Application-Layer Mutation Queue (outbox sync)
nodes.rationale: Sync happens through the existing idempotent API, not a DB sync engine: ElectricSQL/PowerSync would stream rows past the domain rules (withdrawal enforcement, validation, allocation) that live in the .NET API. Client keeps an IndexedDB cache + outbox; each mutation carries a client-generated UUID Idempotency-Key reused on every retry, with the daily-entry natural-key uniqueness as the server backstop. CRDTs rejected — daily entry is single-writer per natural key.

nodes.label: Offline Conflict Resolution (state-machine keyed)
nodes.rationale: Conflicts keyed on the daily-entry state machine: no server entry → accept; server DRAFT with matching baseVersion → accept; stale baseVersion → last-write-wins surfacing superseded values for review; SUBMITTED/LOCKED → reject and route to the manager_adjusted flow. Per-record status Pending/Synced/Needs review; no silent data loss.

nodes.label: ASP.NET Identity + JWT behind IIdentityProvider (KD-5)
nodes.rationale: Identity in the same Postgres issuing short-lived JWT access + rotating refresh tokens, behind an IIdentityProvider port so swapping to Keycloak/Entra later is a new implementation, not domain changes. Frontend keeps the access token in memory and the refresh token in a secure httpOnly cookie to avoid localStorage token theft. Keycloak/Auth0 rejected now: extra infra or per-MAU cost and a cloud tie for barn-side login.
nodes.community_name: SPA Auth Flow (memory token + cookie refresh)

nodes.label: OpenAPI-Generated Typed Client (KD-6)
nodes.rationale: TypeScript client + DTO types generated from the API's OpenAPI document on every build recover Blazor's shared-types benefit: a backend contract change breaking the frontend becomes a compile error, not a runtime surprise. CI diffs the OpenAPI doc to catch accidental breaking changes.

nodes.label: Provider-Agnostic EF Core Strategy (KD-2)
nodes.rationale: Postgres primary; swapping providers is a deliberate tested task, not a runtime switch. No jsonb/arrays/hstore, no provider-specific raw SQL outside ports, concurrency tokens via EF abstraction, migrations per provider in separate assemblies selected by Database:Provider config. Integration tests run real Postgres via Testcontainers because SQLite semantics hide real bugs.

nodes.label: Background Jobs (PeriodicTimer + durable jobs table)
nodes.rationale: BackgroundService + PeriodicTimer sweeping a durable jobs table; tenant-aware and idempotent. No scheduler library — plain .NET primitives cover simple periodic sweeps; multi-instance duplication handled by claim-on-pull (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED). Quartz.NET only earns a place if complex cron, user-editable schedules, or clustered misfire recovery materialize.

nodes.label: Sale-Confirmation Transaction (pessimistic lock)
nodes.rationale: The sale-confirmation handler implements functional §10.9.1 exactly: BEGIN, SELECT egg_lots FOR UPDATE, re-read, validate, insert allocations + movements, update balance + version, COMMIT (conflict → 409). Pessimistic here is deliberate; everywhere else is optimistic concurrency.

nodes.label: i18n Key Naming (namespace:camelCaseKey)
nodes.rationale: Namespaces by area (common, auth, account, sales, errors keyed by stable API error codes, enums via typed helpers). t() for plain strings; <Trans> only when interleaving JSX, with ns prop + unprefixed i18nKey (react-i18next 17 typing quirk).

nodes.label: Hardcoded-String Scan (count ratchet)
nodes.rationale: npm run i18n:scan (scripts/i18n-scan.mjs) is a grep-level scanner flagging un-externalized JSX text and literal attribute values; always exits 0 — a reporting aid, not a CI gate. Convention: each sweep batch's PR reports the count for its scope and the count must not increase (ratchets like the coverage floors). Intentional survivors go in the allowlist; allowlisting an unswept screen's real string would hide the exact regression the tool exists to catch.

nodes.label: Pastel-Mesh Gradient (depth without shadows)
nodes.rationale: Peach/lavender/dusty-green radial-gradient stacks behind hero bands provide the brand's depth language; product UI mockups float above, never inside chrome — the gradient does the lifting instead of shadows.

nodes.label: SPA Auth Flow (memory token + cookie refresh)
nodes.rationale: Access token in JS memory only; refresh token an HttpOnly cookie (#145). 401 triggers one transparent single-flight refresh + retry; page load restores the session by silent refresh. Cross-tab refresh serialised via Web Locks (#169) with a bounded-timeout abort; the tab-closed-mid-refresh residual is covered server-side by the idempotency grace (#176).

nodes.label: AGENTS.md — Cluckwork Agent Brief
nodes.rationale: Shared brief for any coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) on the Cluckwork poultry egg-farm management system: .NET 10 layered DDD backend, React 19 + Vite SPA, Postgres via EF Core.

nodes.label: Layered DDD Architecture
nodes.rationale: Dependencies point inward: Api -> Application/Infrastructure -> Domain; Domain depends on nothing.

nodes.label: Result Pattern
nodes.rationale: Domain/handlers return Result / Result<T> (Domain/Common). Don't throw for expected failures; throw only for invariant violations (e.g. Flock.Create guards).

nodes.label: Version Concurrency Token Convention
nodes.rationale: Every aggregate mutation must bump Version. EF puts the original value in the UPDATE WHERE but never auto-increments, so a mutation without Version++ silently loses concurrent races instead of 409ing. Bug shipped three times (Submit/Lock, SalesOrder.AddItem); each mutation now needs a parallel-race integration test.

nodes.label: Handler per Feature (No MediatR)
nodes.rationale: Handlers invoked directly from endpoints — no MediatR. Handlers/validators/repos registered in Program.cs.

nodes.label: FluentValidation Validation
nodes.rationale: One *Validator per command; endpoints call ValidateAsync and return ValidationProblem.

nodes.label: Minimal API Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Minimal APIs grouped under /api/v1/... via Map<Feature>Endpoints; writes require auth plus an Idempotency-Key (middleware).

nodes.label: Multi-Tenancy Enforcement
nodes.rationale: Every tenant-owned entity has AccountId, enforced by an EF global query filter plus TenantStampInterceptor (stamps on insert). TenantContext resolved per-request from the JWT account_id claim; unresolved at startup, so seeders must use IgnoreQueryFilters().

nodes.label: Asymmetric JWT Auth
nodes.rationale: Asymmetric JWT with rotating refresh tokens. PEM keys come from config with escaped \n; normalize via PemKey.Normalize before ImportFromPem.

nodes.label: Migrations Auto-Apply + DatabaseSeeder
nodes.rationale: EF migrations auto-apply on startup (Database:MigrateOnStartup, default true). DatabaseSeeder seeds default account + admin user + Admin role; credentials only from Seed:* config, never a fallback secret; failures log and skip rather than crash.

nodes.label: Integration Tests via Testcontainers
nodes.rationale: Integration tests spin up a real Postgres via Testcontainers (docker required). No SQLite — EF SQL semantics differ.

nodes.label: Secrets Never Committed Policy
nodes.rationale: deploy/.env gitignored; local API debug config via dotnet user-secrets; no hardcoded passwords/keys — GitGuardian scans PRs; generate test credentials at runtime.

nodes.label: Opt-In Pre-Commit Hook
nodes.rationale: ~2s hook via core.hooksPath .githooks: unit tests for staged .cs changes, npm run typecheck for staged web/ changes. Integration tests deliberately excluded (Docker, slow) — CI is the authority.

nodes.label: CI Security Gates (#146)
nodes.rationale: CI fails a PR on known high+ advisories: NuGet via dotnet list package --vulnerable (parsed; CLI always exits 0), npm production deps via npm audit --omit=dev. Dev-only advisories are advisory-only since they don't ship to users. CodeQL is advisory SAST; a scheduled weekly audit catches advisories published while no PR is open.

nodes.label: NuGet Lock Files Convention
nodes.rationale: Directory.Build.props sets RestorePackagesWithLockFile; every project commits packages.lock.json and CI restores with --locked-mode so restores are deterministic and deps can't float between local and CI. Bumping a package without committing refreshed lock files fails CI with NU1004.

nodes.label: Dependency Submission Workflow
nodes.rationale: GitHub parses .csproj/.nuspec manifests for NuGet, never packages.lock.json, so it sees ~20 direct PackageReferences of ~80 resolved — dependency-review is blind to transitive vulnerable packages. dependency-submission.yml closes this: component-detection reads restore output and submits the resolved graph via the Dependency Submission API. npm needs none of this (web/package-lock.json is read natively).

nodes.label: Dependabot Lock-File Healing Workflow
nodes.rationale: Dependabot regenerates only the bumped project's packages.lock.json; downstream projects then fail --locked-mode with NU1004. dependabot-lockfix.yml re-runs dotnet restore --force-evaluate in a no-credential job, then commits/pushes refreshed lock files from a separate job that runs no project code and holds a short-lived GitHub App token. Fails closed until LOCKFIX_APP_ID/LOCKFIX_APP_PRIVATE_KEY secrets exist.

nodes.label: Security Exceptions Escape Hatch
nodes.rationale: .github/security-exceptions.json mutes one advisory (exact GHSA id, ecosystem, reason, required expiry date) until the date passes. vuln-gate.mjs fails closed on malformed reports/exceptions. The same file feeds dependency-review's allowlist so the gates never disagree. Prefer bumping or pinning a patched version over an exception.

nodes.label: Dependabot Configuration
nodes.rationale: The gates enforce (a vulnerable dep fails the build), Dependabot proposes (opens bump PRs, flags new advisories day-of). Neither replaces the other. Weekly grouped version updates for github-actions, npm (web/), nuget; security fixes arrive ungrouped.

nodes.label: Git / PR Workflow
nodes.rationale: origin = GitHub, gitea = backup mirror. main is protected — branch and PR, squash-merge, commit/push only when the human asks. Phase epic checklists (#14 = Phase 1.1, #15 = Phase 1.5) must be kept in sync when filing slice issues; milestones alone are not enough.

nodes.label: Documentation-in-Sync Directive
